questions.q: According to the passage, what were the Luddites mainly doing?
options: Fighting as irregular militias against French forces during the Napoleonic Wars
Organizing legal strikes backed by trade unions to win higher wages
Using machine-breaking to pressure employers over pay and working conditions
Opposing every new technology on principle, much like modern critics of progress
questions.explain: They attacked machines as leverage; many were skilled operators not opposed to machines per se.

questions.q: Where and when did the Luddite movement begin?
questions.explain: The movement began in Arnold, Nottinghamshire, on 11 March 1811.

questions.q: What was the hammer used by Yorkshire croppers called?
questions.explain: They called it Enoch to mock Enoch Taylor, the cropping machine maker.

questions.q: Which event is described as the last major Luddite act?
questions.explain: Jeremiah Brandreth's Pentrich Rising in 1817 can be viewed as the last major Luddite act.

questions.q: What did Eric Hobsbawm mean by 'collective bargaining by riot'?
options: Luddites negotiated directly with mill owners while threatening to smash their machines at night
Union leaders organized riots to force Parliament to repeal laws against organized labor
Machine-wrecking was a substitute for large strikes that were impractical as factories were scattered
Rioting was tolerated by magistrates as a legal way for workers to petition for higher pay
questions.explain: Hobsbawm said manufactories were scattered, making large-scale strikes impractical.
